stories.headline: Border fence removed as Spain, Gibraltar mark historic agreement
stories.summary: Spain and Gibraltar have removed the border fence and lifted controls at their frontier following a UK-EU agreement that allows free movement between the two territories. The change resolves a long-standing dispute over Gibraltar's status and enables residents and visitors to cross without checkpoints for the first time in decades.

angles.headline: Watch: Celebrations as Gibraltar-Spain border fence removed
angles.summary: Spain and Gibraltar have removed the border fence and lifted controls at their frontier following a UK-EU agreement that allows free movement between the two territories. The change resolves a long-standing dispute over Gibraltar's status and enables residents and visitors to cross without checkpoints for the first time in decades.

angles.headline: A special team beats brilliant individuals - how silky Spain flattened France
angles.summary: Spain defeats France in the World Cup semifinal through coordinated team play, advancing to the championship match. The victory demonstrates how cohesive tactical execution can overcome individual star talent, recalling Spain's dominant 2010 World Cup campaign.

angles.headline: Seven Britons among those killed in Spain wildfires
angles.summary: Wildfires in Spain have killed at least 13 people, including seven British nationals and five other foreign visitors. The deaths highlight how rapidly spreading fires in popular tourist regions can trap visitors who may be unfamiliar with evacuation routes and local hazards.

stories.headline: Iran threatens to block more trade routes as US launches fresh strikes
stories.summary: The US and Iran are engaged in escalating military strikes and counter-strikes, with the US resuming a blockade of Iranian ports while Iran threatens to disrupt shipping through critical waterways like the Strait of Hormuz. These tit-for-tat actions reflect deepening tensions that complicate regional security and global trade flows through one of the world's most economically vital shipping channels.

stories.headline: New US Ebola patient arrives in Germany for treatment
stories.summary: A second American infected with Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo has been evacuated to Germany for specialized medical care. The transfer reflects both the severity of the patient's condition and international protocols for treating infectious diseases in equipped facilities, occurring as the outbreak in eastern Congo has grown beyond official tracking capacity.

stories.headline: T.Rex skeleton sells for $50.1 million at New York auction
stories.summary: A nearly complete Tyrannosaurus rex skeleton nicknamed "Gus" sold for $50.1 million at a Sotheby's auction in New York, setting a record price for any dinosaur fossil ever sold. The skeleton, which stands over 13 feet tall and dates back approximately 67 million years, had been estimated to fetch between $15 million and $25 million before the sale.

stories.headline: Bangkok pub fire death toll rises to 32 with 15 in intensive care
stories.summary: A fire at a Bangkok pub kills 32 people and injures dozens more, with 15 victims requiring intensive care treatment. Authorities are investigating negligence as the likely cause while questions emerge about recurring safety failures in Thailand's entertainment venues.

stories.headline: FIFA World Cup: England vs Argentina prediction, schedule, road to final
stories.summary: England and Argentina prepare to face each other in a World Cup semifinal, with both teams arriving after distinct tournament paths and carrying decades of sporting rivalry. The match carries particular intensity due to the nations' historical tensions both on the pitch and off, adding weight to what is already football's highest stage.

stories.headline: China’s economy grows at 4.3%, one of its lowest rates on record
stories.summary: China's economy expanded 4.3% in the latest period, reflecting structural slowdowns from weak domestic demand and a struggling property sector. The growth rate ranks among the lowest in recent decades, prompting concerns within Beijing about sustaining employment and meeting development goals.

stories.headline: Three killed as Russian bombing of Odesa continues
stories.summary: Russian airstrikes on the Ukrainian port city of Odesa have killed three people as part of an intensifying campaign over control of the Black Sea. Ukraine has responded with attacks on Russian vessels in the region, reflecting the strategic importance of maritime routes and military assets in the conflict.

stories.headline: How the failed 2016 coup reshaped Turkiye’s civil-military relations
stories.summary: Turkey's military underwent significant institutional transformation following the 2016 coup attempt, as the government restructured command hierarchies and removed thousands of officers suspected of disloyalty. The crackdown extended far beyond military ranks, ensnaring cadets and civilians in a sweeping purge that fundamentally altered the balance of power between Turkey's armed forces and civilian leadership.

stories.headline: Volodymyr Zelenskyy pushes for new government in Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy initiates a government reshuffle as Parliament accepts Prime Minister Svyrydenko's resignation with 258 votes. The restructuring reflects shifting priorities in Ukraine's leadership during the ongoing conflict, with attention turning to the defence ministry's role in the war effort.
